THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 -3-  NC: 2023:KHC-K:5521  MFA No.200467 of 2018  C/W MFA No.201705 of 2018 Kavita vs Sandesh And Anr on 19 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180098260/
2  JUDGMENT MFA No.200467/2018

is filed by the insurer challenging the liability imposed upon it to pay compensation as well as the rate of interest awarded by the Member, MACT-XIII and IV Additional District Judge, Kalaburagi (henceforth referred to as 'the Tribunal'), in MVC No.1358/2015 vide judgment and award dated 08.12.2017.
2. MFA No.201705/2018 is filed by the claimant seeking enhancement of compensation awarded by the Tribunal in the aforesaid case.
3. A claim petition was filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation for the injuries suffered by the claimant in a road traffic accident on 13.05.2011.

The claimant claimed that when she was walking by the side of the road along with her neighbour, a multi utility vehicle bearing registration No.MH-08-W-0429 (henceforth referred to as the 'offending vehicle') dashed against her, resulting in injuries to her.

She was shifted to Rural hospital,
Sangameshwar, Dist. Ratnagiri and thereafter to Miraj hospital, for treatment.
She also availed treatment at Dr. Deshpande's NC: 2023:KHC-K:5521 hospital, Vijayapur where she underwent surgery for fixing the fracture of right shaft of the femur.
The claimant claimed that she was 18 years old and a labourer earning Rs.6,000/- per month.
She claimed that due to the injuries, she was disabled and hence, sought compensation from the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle.
4. Insurer contested the claim petition and denied the accident as well as the entitlement of the claimant for the compensation.
It claimed that the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess a valid licence to drive the offending vehicle.
5. Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
The claimant was examined as P.W.1 and she marked documents Exs.P.1 to P.13.

She examined a doctor as P.W.2.
who deposed that the claimant had suffered disability to the extent of 28% to the right lower limb.
The insurer examined one of its officials as R.W.1 and marked Exs.R1 to R.3.
6.

Based on the oral and documentary evidence adduced before the Tribunal, the Tribunal held that accident NC: 2023:KHC-K:5521 occurred due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle.
It also held that the claimant suffered fracture of the right shaft femur as well as fracture of left clavicle.
It noticed that the claimant had availed treatment at various hospitals between 14.05.2011 and 27.05.2011.
It considered the evidence of P.W.2 and held that the claimant had suffered disability to the extent of 8% to the whole body.

It considered the notional income of the claimant at a sum of Rs.30,000/- per annum as per the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Kishan Gopal and Another vs. Lala and Others1 since it found that the claimant was 17 years old as per the discharge card at Ex.P.7 and awarded the following compensation:
 Sl. Heads Amount  No. (In Rs.)
 1. Medical expenses 55,000/-
 2. Pain and suffering 25,000/-
 3. Loss of amenities 15,000/-

It directed the insurer to pay the compensation along with interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization.
Being aggrieved by the same, the insurer as well as the claimant are in appeals.

8. Learned counsel for the insurer submitted that the owner did not intimate the insurer about the accident and though the insurer issued notice calling upon the owner to furnish the details of licence of the driver, the owner failed to do so even after the receipt of the notice.
Therefore, an adverse inference deserves to be drawn in the case against the owner.
Consequently, she contended that the liability imposed upon the insurer to pay the compensation be modified and the insurer be permitted to pay and recover the compensation awarded.
She also contended that the Tribunal awarded 9% interest though there was no justifiable circumstance to do so.

9. Per contra, learned counsel for the claimant contended that the claimant had not only suffered fracture of right shaft of femur, but also fracture of left clavicle which was not considered by the Tribunal.
He contended that the claimant was a labourer and the same is evidenced from the complaint NC: 2023:KHC-K:5521 at Ex.P.2 as well as panchanama at Ex.P.3,
He therefore,

contended that the fracture of right femur and clavicle had rendered the claimant totally disabled and therefore, the Tribunal must have considered the disability suffered by the claimant as well as the bodily function that were affected.
He therefore, prays that the disability assessed by the Tribunal be re-considered.

He also contended that the Tribunal considered the age of the claimant at 17 years based on Ex.P.7 while the claimant was 22 years old and she adduced evidence as P.W.1 and stated that she was 22 years old at the time of deposition before the Court i.e., on 10.11.2016.
He therefore, contended that the Tribunal committed an error in considering the annual notional income of the claimant at a sum of Rs.30,000/-.

He submitted that the this Court in similar circumstances, considered the notional income at a sum of Rs.6,000/- per month and hence, prayed that the compensation be re- determined by considering the notional income at a sum of Rs.6,000/-
per month.
10. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the claimant as well as the learned counsel for the insurer.

4 NC: 2023:KHC-K:5521 11.
It is seen from the wound certificate at Ex.P.5 that the claimant not only suffered fracture of right shaft femur, but also left clavicle.
The claimant claimed that she was a labourer and therefore, the injuries must have left her disabled not only in the right lower limb but also in the upper limb.
Therefore, the disability assessed by the Tribunal at 8% deserves to be enhanced to 12%.
The accident in question happened on 13.05.2011.
When the claimant deposed before the Court in the year 2016, she claimed that she was 22 years old.
Therefore, it is more than probable that the claimant was 17 years old girl at the time of the accident.

Having regard to the fact that this Court had considered the disability suffered by the claimant at 12%, following the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Master Mallikarjun vs. Divisional Manager, National Insurance Company Limited2, the claimant would be entitled to the following compensation:
(2014) 14 SCC 396 NC: 2023:KHC-K:5521 Sl. Heads Amount No. (In Rs.)
1. Pain and suffering 3,00,000/-
2.

3. Inconvenience caused to the 25,000/-
 parents during  hospitalization  4.

As regards the liability to pay the compensation is concerned, though the insurer contended that the adverse inference deserves to be drawn against the owner, the evidence on record does not show any efforts by the insurer to establish that the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess a valid licence to drive the offending vehicle.
It also does not show that the insurer made any attempts before the Court to summon the owner of the offending vehicle to produce the licence.
In the absence of this, the insurer cannot expect the Court to draw an adverse inference against the owner and seek liberty to pay and recover the compensation from the owner.
In that view of the matter, the insurer is liable to pay the compensation determined by this Court along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization.

5 13.
In view of the above, MFA No.201705/2018 filed by the claimant is allowed in part.
The compensation of Rs.1,45,000/- awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced to Rs.4,00,000/-.
14. MFA No.200467/2018 filed by the insurer is allowed in part, in so far as it relates to rate of interest is concerned.

15. The insurer is directed to pay compensation along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petitions till the date of realization.
16.
The insurer shall deposit the compensation along with interest before the Tribunal within a period of one month from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
17. Upon deposit, 50% of the compensation and accrued interest shall be kept in the name of claimant in a fixed deposit in any nationalized bank for a period of three years.
18. Any amount in deposit is ordered to be transferred to the Tribunal for necessary orders.
